evidence.intree_statement: Program Definition Groupoid (C : Category) : Category := {| obj := @obj C; hom := @Isomorphism C; homset := @iso_setoid C; id := @iso_id C; compose := @iso_compose C |}

statement_record.book: The inclusion Groupoid ↪ Cat admits both a left and a right adjoint: the right adjoint sends a category to its maximal subgroupoid (functors out of a groupoid preserve isomorphisms, hence factor uniquely through the core), and the left adjoint formally inverts every morphism, giving the category of fractions built as a quotient of the free category on the quiver of C glued to that of C^op, with zig-zags modulo the two cancellation relations.
statement_record.intree: Groupoid C is the core, built objectwise: objects @obj C, homs @Isomorphism C, identity iso_id, composition iso_compose, morphism equivalence @iso_setoid C.

Neither adjunction is stated, and the library itself discloses this at Construction/Groupoid.v:93-95 ('The file constructs the core of a given C; no standalone category of groupoids exists in-tree, so the adjunction remark in the header above remains prose rather than a theorem'). The left adjoint has no counterpart at all.

statement_record.book: Given F : C → D, G : D → C and a family of bijections D(Fc,d) ≅ C(c,Gd) NOT assumed natural, prove that naturality of the family is equivalent to: for all h : c' → c, k : d → d', f♯ : Fc → d, g♯ : Fc' → d', the square in D with sides Fh, f♯, g♯, k commutes iff the transposed square in C with sides h, f♭, g♭, Gk commutes.
statement_record.intree: The two naturality directions are the class fields verbatim (⌊f ∘ fmap[F] g⌋ ≈ ⌊f⌋ ∘ g and ⌊f ∘ g⌋ ≈ fmap[U] f ∘ ⌊g⌋); from them Comma_Functor_F_Id_Id_G / Comma_Functor_Id_G_F_Id transport commuting squares in both directions and Comma_F_Id_Id_G_Iso shows the transport is a bijection; Adjunction_Comma packages the two-way statement as F ⊣ G ↔ lawvere_equiv.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on the converse leg. Forward (naturality ⟹ square correspondence) is fully in-tree and in fact stronger than asked, since the correspondence is upgraded to an isomorphism of comma categories. The converse in-tree is NOT 'square correspondence ⟹ naturality': `lawvere_equiv` (Construction/Comma/Adjunction.v:83) demands more than a square-respecting bijection — besides the comma iso it carries projF, projG (the iso lies over D ∏ C) AND the extra whisker coherence field σ : whisker_equiv … relating the iso's unit/counit to the projection comparison cells κ, θ. So the backward implication is proved under strictly stronger hypotheses than Riehl's.

gap: No in-tree lemma quantifies over an ARBITRARY (not-assumed-natural) family of hom-set bijections adj{x,y} : (F x ~> y) ≊ (x ~> U y) and proves the biconditional 'naturality ⟺ commuting squares correspond'. In-tree, naturality is a definitional FIELD of the Adjunction class, so the direction the exercise asks about (square correspondence ⇒ naturality, a one-line specialization taking g♯ := k ∘ f♯ ∘ fmap[F] h) is never stated; the only converse available, Adjunction_Comma's ← branch, additionally requires the projF/projG over-D∏C data and the whisker_equiv coherence σ. statement_record.book: Any adjoint triple L ⊣ U ⊣ R between C and D gives rise to a canonical adjunction LU ⊣ RU between the induced endofunctors of C, and an adjunction UL ⊣ UR between the induced endofunctors of D.
statement_record.intree: Adjunction_Compose : (F' ◯ F) ⊣ (U ◯ U') from A : F ⊣ U and A' : F' ⊣ U' — adjunctions compose, in the hom-set presentation by pasting the two transposing isomorphisms in Sets (adj_compose_iso := iso_compose (adj A) (adj A')), with all four naturality fields populated.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger as a general law (arbitrary composable adjunctions, both transposes' naturality, plus the whiskering formulas Adjunction_Compose_unit/counit), but the exercise's two conclusions are not instantiated. Feeding U ⊣ R then L ⊣ U into Adjunction_Compose yields L◯U ⊣ R◯U on C, and feeding L ⊣ U then U ⊣ R yields U◯L ⊣ U◯R on D; neither instantiation is written down.

statement_record.book: If F : C ⇄ D : G with F ⊣ G, then the comma categories F ↓ D and C ↓ G (formed from F and G against the identity functors) are isomorphic, via an isomorphism commuting with the forgetful functors to C × D.
statement_record.intree: Comma_F_Id_Id_G_Iso (H : F ⊣ G) : (F ↓ Id[C]) ≅[Cat] (Id[D] ↓ G), acting as ((d,c); f) ↦ ((d,c); ⌊f⌋) and ((d,c); g) ↦ ((d,c); ⌈g⌉); Adjunction_Comma's forward branch upgrades this to a `lawvere_equiv`, whose projF/projG fields state precisely that the iso and its inverse commute with comma_proj : Comma ⟶ D ∏ C.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger: the exercise asks only for the forward implication, while Adjunction_Comma proves the biconditional (Lawvere's theorem), reconstructing the adjunction from a comma isomorphism over D ∏ C via lawvere_eqv_unit_transform / lawvere_eqv_counit_transform and the two triangle identities. The commuting-with-the-projections clause the exercise demands is exactly projF/projG, and the identity-on-(d,c) object action of the two comparison functors makes it visible directly; the only difference in presentation is the product order (D ∏ C rather than C × D) and the use of Lemma 4.1.3's naturality via the to_adj_nat_*/from_adj_nat_* fields, which is how the square obligations are discharged.
